value: *** THE TWO SOUTH AFRICAN DEATH RECORDS BOTH MAKE HIM MID-SEVENTIES. *** The death NOTICE says "77 years - approx". The death CERTIFICATE says "76 years". A birth of 16 August 1872 makes him 77 at his death on 19 March 1950.
note: *** The Argentine passport's 22 February 1882 makes him 68. The gap is nine years and it is not a rounding. ***

value: *** THE NAMES. *** ROBERTO - he died as Robert Paul. JUAN - his second son was Ricardo JUAN Carlos, and the enrolment card names his father Juan Carlos. ROQUE - his eldest son was ROQUE Luis Armando.
note: Three given names, three echoes. Argentine naming is repetitive and this proves nothing on its own, but it is the reason somebody pulled the image.

value: The death certificate registers him as *** LERINA *** and gives his birthplace only as *** "SOUTH AMERICA" *** - not Argentina, not Rosario. The death notice says only "Argentine".
note: *** Neither South African document was completed by family. *** The notice was signed by Rose Lilian Theys, no relation; the certificate by W. Fraser, whose qualification is "causing burial" - an undertaker. Nobody who knew him supplied any of it.

value: LLORENS and LERENA are not far apart in a Spanish-speaking mouth written down by an English-speaking clerk, and this family's surname is already documented as Lerena, Llerena, Lorena, Larena and Lerina.
note: Weak. Llorens is Catalan and ends in -s; Lerena does not. Recorded as the weakest of the four.

value: *** HIS OWN PASSPORT, WHICH HE SIGNED. *** Argentine passport Serie A no. 07962, Cape Town consulate, 24 December 1940: born ROSARIO DE SANTA FE, 22 February 1882. He signed it "P. A. Lerena" and put his right thumbprint on it.
note: *** This is the only document in the whole question filled in by the man himself. ***

value: *** THE 1908 ENROLMENT CARD. *** Clase de 1882. Nacido en Rosario de Santa Fe. Hijo de Juan Carlos Lerena y de Maria Lerena.
note: Filed in his own name, in Argentina, in his twenties - and it agrees with the passport thirty-two years later.

value: *** THE PARENTS DO NOT MATCH AT ALL. *** Roberto Llorens and Francisca Fernandez, both Spanish-born, against Juan Carlos Lerena and Maria Lerena.
note: Not a variant spelling. Different names, different people.

value: *** THE PLACE DOES NOT MATCH. *** Buenos Aires against Rosario de Santa Fe, three hundred kilometres apart, and the passport names Rosario in his own hand.
*** NOT THE SAME MAN, ON THE EVIDENCE AS IT STANDS - AND THE AGE PROBLEM IS REAL AND IS NOT DISMISSED. ***
note: Two documents he completed himself say 1882 and Rosario. Two documents completed by strangers after his death say mid-seventies. *** The simplest reading is that a landlady and an undertaker guessed his age high, which is exactly what strangers do. *** The alternative - that he shaved nine years off himself in Argentina and kept the lie for thirty-two years, including on a consular passport where he produced no birth certificate - is not impossible and is why this file is kept open rather than closed.

value: *** The Llorens family is traceable and this archive has not spent an hour on it. *** Look for Roberto Juan Roque Llorens after 1872 in Buenos Aires: a marriage, a military enrolment, a death. If he lived and died in Argentina, the question closes in an afternoon. *** That is the cheapest open question in this archive. ***
